I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 10, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in winter, so hunting and the company's stores carry us until spring planting. The ground here gives a long growing season on thin soil. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winters are mild, so my worry is drought, heat waves and wood running short. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is heat waves and thin wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Recovery. If the food runs out, it is the top of the ladder. I pause, check every stockpile and the freezer with game_state, then game_set cmd hunt on everything safe nearby, pick berries and anything edible, and drop the meal bill to simple meals only so nothing is wasted on fine meals. Fields close to camp get the fastest crop, and nobody eats a raw corpse while we can cook.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

messages.content: You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: tropical rainforest, flat terrain, Randy Random on Strive to Survive, 2 colonists with nobody with medical skill, landing in fall, company start. And tell me how you recover if half the crew downed.

Here is my plan for this one, start to finish.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is tropical rainforest on a flat tile with no rock to hide behind, so the perimeter wall does all the work, with Randy Random on Strive to Survive: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Some facility doors start sealed, and those rooms often hold the shelves, beds and benches I need, so I never skip them. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: capybaras, monkeys and boomalopes, and fruit everywhere. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade and Mira, nobody with medical skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: tundra, mountainous terrain, Randy Random on Community Builder, 1 colonist with nobody with medical skill, landing in spring, company start. And tell me how you recover if food gone.

Here is the whole run, in order, the way I play it every time.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is tundra on a mountainous tile, so the facility backs onto rock and the mountain base comes later, with Randy Random on Community Builder: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: caribou, muffalo and arctic foxes, almost no wild plants. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, nobody with medical skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade carries everything, so every column after Cooking gets a 2 or 3 in the order the day needs, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a doctor, so doctoring stays at 1 for all and I keep medicine at Best so the low skill is offset by good kits, and I research and recruit for a doctor early. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives only a few warm weeks to grow in. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. It is cold almost all year, so heaters, insulated walls and hydroponics are the real winter plan, and hunting is the backbone of the larder. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is year-round cold and very little wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Recovery. If the food runs out, it is the top of the ladder. I pause, check every stockpile and the freezer with game_state, then game_set cmd hunt on everything safe nearby, pick berries and anything edible, and drop the meal bill to simple meals only so nothing is wasted on fine meals. Fields close to camp get the fastest crop, and nobody eats a raw corpse while we can cook.

Same order every time: explore, set pawns, set stores, then time, then the empire.

messages.content: You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: ice sheet, large hills terrain, Randy Random on Losing is Fatal, 3 colonists with nobody with medical skill, landing in spring, company start. And tell me how you recover if base on fire.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is ice sheet on a large-hills tile, with some stone to mine and some open ground to farm, with Randy Random on Losing is Fatal: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Some facility doors start sealed, and those rooms often hold the shelves, beds and benches I need, so I never skip them. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: arctic foxes, arctic hares and the odd muffalo herd are the only food that walks. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira and Tobin, nobody with medical skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a doctor, so doctoring stays at 1 for all and I keep medicine at Best so the low skill is offset by good kits, and I research and recruit for a doctor early. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I tell the stream with say that the setup is finished and the clock is running. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives no soil and no outdoor growing at all. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Rice for rice in hydroponics, and a second plot of potato as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. There is no summer to wait for: power, heaters and hydroponics basins under sun lamps are survival, not luxury. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is no soil, no trees and lethal cold, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Recovery. If the base catches fire, firefighting is already a 1 for everyone, so the crew answers it. I pause, look at where it spreads, and pull the stores out of the burning rooms first. Then I rebuild the burnt walls in stone, and add firebreaks so it cannot happen the same way again.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: tropical rainforest, mountainous terrain, Cassandra Classic on Losing is Fatal, 3 colonists with nobody with any cooking skill, landing in fall, company start, and plague early.

Here is my plan for this one, start to finish.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is tropical rainforest on a mountainous tile, so the facility backs onto rock and the mountain base comes later, with Cassandra Classic on Losing is Fatal: steady, rising threats with breathing room between them. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: capybaras, monkeys and boomalopes, and fruit everywhere. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira and Tobin, nobody with any cooking skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody can really cook, so cooking stays at 1 for everyone like always and the best of a bad lot cooks; the kitchen gets a smooth floor kept clean so food poisoning stays rare. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in fall, so I plant the fastest crop now and hunt hard before winter. The ground here gives growing all year round. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Rice for rice, and a second plot of potato as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. Plague shows up in the first month. Plague is a race between immunity and the disease, so the sick go straight to bed, the doctor tends them with the best medicine twice a day, and the healthy ones feed them. Good food and a clean hospital push the odds our way.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. There is no winter, but diseases are common and food rots fast in the heat, so the freezer and the doctor matter more than the heater. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is diseases and fast rot, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

That is the run: read the facility, set the people, set the stores, then let time move, and grow until the whole map is ours.

You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: temperate forest, large hills terrain, Phoebe Chillax on Losing is Fatal, 3 colonists with one pacifist who will not fight, landing in summer, company start, and raid on day 3 early.

Here is the whole run, in order, the way I play it every time.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is temperate forest on a large-hills tile, with some stone to mine and some open ground to farm, with Phoebe Chillax on Losing is Fatal: long quiet stretches, so I use the quiet to build hard. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: deer, boar and muffalo wander through, and berries grow wild. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira and Tobin, one pacifist who will not fight. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. One colonist is a pacifist, so hunting goes on the others and the pacifist takes growing, hauling and the kitchen; in a fight they stay inside and fight fires. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 15, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I tell the stream with say that the setup is finished and the clock is running. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives a long growing season with a real winter. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Rice for rice, and a second plot of potato as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. A raid letter lands on day three. A raid on day three is early, so the prisoner bed goes down that same hour. I do not draft while the raiders are still off the map preparing; I keep everyone working, give every pawn a weapon, and only draft once a hostile is actually on the map. We fight from inside the facility doorway, then field-tend the downed raiders, capture one, and do the after-the-fight list straight away: close open rooms, get loot inside, stores and the cooler right.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winter here drops below freezing for most of a quadrum, so the fields die off and the freezer and the hay stock carry us. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Electricity comes first in research, typed into the search box, then generators that stand outside the walls. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is fires in summer and the odd manhunter pack, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

That is the run: read the facility, set the people, set the stores, then let time move, and grow until the whole map is ours.

You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.
Walk me through a full run: arid shrubland, large hills terrain, Randy Random on Strive to Survive, 2 colonists with nobody with any cooking skill, landing in fall, company start.

Here is the whole run, in order, the way I play it every time.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is arid shrubland on a large-hills tile, with some stone to mine and some open ground to farm, with Randy Random on Strive to Survive: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: gazelle, dromedaries and agave in the brush. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade and Mira, nobody with any cooking skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody can really cook, so cooking stays at 1 for everyone like always and the best of a bad lot cooks; the kitchen gets a smooth floor kept clean so food poisoning stays rare. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 10, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in fall, so I plant the fastest crop now and hunt hard before winter. The ground here gives a long growing season on thin soil. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winters are mild, so my worry is drought, heat waves and wood running short. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is heat waves and thin wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Same order every time: explore, set pawns, set stores, then time, then the empire.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is tundra on a large-hills tile, with some stone to mine and some open ground to farm, with Phoebe Chillax on Strive to Survive: long quiet stretches, so I use the quiet to build hard. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Some facility doors start sealed, and those rooms often hold the shelves, beds and benches I need, so I never skip them. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: caribou, muffalo and arctic foxes, almost no wild plants. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade and Mira, nobody with medical skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a doctor, so doctoring stays at 1 for all and I keep medicine at Best so the low skill is offset by good kits, and I research and recruit for a doctor early. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives only a few warm weeks to grow in. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. A cold snap hits in the middle of the growing season. A cold snap freezes crops dead, so the moment the letter arrives I harvest everything that is close to ready, light heaters or campfires indoors, and make sure every pawn has a warm bed and a roof. Then I resow once it lifts.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. It is cold almost all year, so heaters, insulated walls and hydroponics are the real winter plan, and hunting is the backbone of the larder. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is year-round cold and very little wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

That is the run: read the facility, set the people, set the stores, then let time move, and grow until the whole map is ours.

Walk me through a full run: boreal forest, flat terrain, Phoebe Chillax on Losing is Fatal, 3 colonists with nobody who builds well, landing in summer, company start, and toxic fallout early.

Here is the whole run, in order, the way I play it every time.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is boreal forest on a flat tile with no rock to hide behind, so the perimeter wall does all the work, with Phoebe Chillax on Losing is Fatal: long quiet stretches, so I use the quiet to build hard. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Some facility doors start sealed, and those rooms often hold the shelves, beds and benches I need, so I never skip them. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: caribou, elk and hares, plus plenty of wood. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira and Tobin, nobody who builds well. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a good builder, so construction goes at 2 on the steadiest pawn and they train on cheap walls before anything important. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 10, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives a short growing season, maybe half the year. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. Toxic fallout starts in the first season. Toxic fallout means everyone works under a roof. I set the outdoor work to short trips only, harvest anything close to ripe before the fallout kills it, and live off the stores and hunting kills already in the freezer. Indoor jobs, crafting and research carry the colony until it passes.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winter is long and hard here, so I stock at least a full season of meals and firewood before the first frost and put a heater in every room. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Electricity comes first in research, typed into the search box, then generators that stand outside the walls. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is cold snaps that kill crops and long winters, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Same order every time: explore, set pawns, set stores, then time, then the empire.
